text: Suddenly there was a quiet knock. <break time="0.8s" /> At the front door. <break time="0.8s" /> So soft that the old man. <break time="0.8s" /> Hardly heard it. <break time="0.8s" /> The match in his hand went out. <break time="0.8s" /> And when a second knock came. <break time="0.8s" /> He hurried back to the bedroom. <break time="0.8s" /> It is Herbert. <break time="0.8s" /> Cried Missus White. <break time="0.8s" /> Running toward the stairs. <break time="0.8s" /> I forgot that the cemetery. <break time="0.8s" /> Was two miles away. <break time="0.8s" /> Her husband held her arm. <break time="0.8s" /> And begged her not to open the door. <break time="0.8s" /> But she pulled herself away. <break time="0.8s" /> Hurrying down the stairs. <break time="0.8s" /> She tried to pull back the heavy bolt. <break time="0.8s" /> Which was too high for her to reach. <break time="0.8s" /> Meanwhile the old man was on his hands and knees. <break time="0.8s" /> Searching the dark floor. <break time="0.8s" /> For the monkeys paw. <break time="0.8s" /> The knocks grew louder and louder. <break time="0.8s" /> And he heard his wife. <break time="0.8s" /> Drag a chair to the door. <break time="0.8s" /> Just as the bolt began to slide back. <break time="0.8s" /> He found the paw. <break time="0.8s" /> And made his third and last wish. <break time="0.8s" /> At that very moment. <break time="0.8s" /> The knocking stopped. <break time="0.8s" /> Though its sound still seemed. <break time="0.8s" /> To echo through the house. <break time="0.8s" /> The door opened. <break time="0.8s" /> And a cold wind rushed in but the street lamp shone. <break time="0.8s" /> Only on a quiet, empty road.
